note: Forms in the entity seed are the values canonical-operators.json carries for those operators (checked when this file was written). Expected trees come from an independent reference walk of the same rules.

cases.id: the guard (and (= a 1) (not b)) is a series of a block and an invert
a filter with a lambda is a conveyor whose lambda names its parameter
a let names its two bound names and has each value then the body
an if puts its condition at [1] and its branches at .then and .else
an object literal names its member keys beside its children
an operator the table lacks is the explicit form unknown
a types map types the nodes whose path it lists and no others
do puts its steps at .do[i-1] and when its body at .then[i-2]
a list that is not a call is an array of members at [i]
a multi-parameter lambda names every parameter
a string literal keeps its JSON text and a number its digits
a build on a cold atom asks for the std manifest
a manifest naming the operators table asks for it
control: a manifest without orbLanguage operators fails the request

payload.reason: the installed @almadar/std declares no orbLanguage operators

cases.id: control: an unreadable file fails the request and the atom stays cold

payload.reason: the operator table is not readable: ENOENT

cases.id: control: a table that is not JSON fails the request

payload.reason: the operator table is not valid JSON

cases.id: control: a second request while the table loads is refused, not dropped

payload.reason: the operator table is still loading

cases.id: a loaded table fills the forms and the infix operators, reads a missing visual as unknown, and answers the waiting request
a null literal is a literal node, never a dropped expression
a null object member is a literal node, never a dropped member
a later let binding reads an earlier one: its source is that earlier value
an inner let shadows an outer one of the same name: the innermost binding is the source
